# Pages + private RFL — review and migration notes

This adds an opt-in Actions replacement for the site's built-in Jekyll Pages deployment. It preserves the existing Jekyll site, CNAME and recursive public submodules and overlays a verified browser artifact at `/rfl/`. It never checks out the private game source or commits generated files. Interiors is excluded from this RFL release.

The companion private repository contains `.github/workflows/browser-release.yml` and the full [setup, runtime prerequisites, dry-run and rollback guide](https://github.com/KO0I/rasd-fastwalker-league-js/blob/main/release/README.md).

## Credentials and activation

- Public environment `rfl-artifact-read`: secret `RFL_ARTIFACTS_TOKEN`, a fine-grained PAT restricted to private `KO0I/rasd-fastwalker-league-js`, **Actions: read** plus implicit Metadata: read. No Contents permission. This permission covers all Actions artifacts/logs in that one repo, not just one artifact.
- Private environment `rfl-public-handoff`: secret `RFL_SITE_DISPATCH_TOKEN`, restricted to this public repository, **Actions: write** plus implicit Metadata: read. It can invoke site workflows; no Contents permission.
- Restrict public `rfl-artifact-read` and `github-pages` environments to `master`; restrict private `rfl-public-handoff` to `main`. Protect default branches and apply your normal release review.
- Keep public variable `RFL_PAGES_ENABLED` unset/false during review and dry runs. Leave current Pages settings unchanged. Only after approval: choose Pages source **GitHub Actions**, preserve `chipchirp.digital`/HTTPS, and set `RFL_PAGES_ENABLED=true`.
- The public build uses built-in Contents: read. Only the deployment job has Pages: write and ID-token: write. No cross-repository Contents token, no Git write token, no private source checkout, no PR-triggered secret access.

## Safe dry run

Before merging: run `python3 -m unittest discover -s .github/scripts -p 'test_*.py' -v` and `actionlint .github/workflows/pages-with-rfl.yml` locally. The private companion has separate packaging tests and a fail-closed real-asset preflight. Runtime assets have been restored and hash-locked; private preview artifact `11454548481` was built successfully from RFL commit `540daa13815c98051f3ab2a5d1d1a17a0830918f`.

After the reviewed workflows reach their default branches, produce a private `dry_run=true` artifact and record its ID. Manually run this workflow on `master`, `dry_run=true`, `rfl_artifact_id=<that ID>`. This builds and validates the full site on the runner without uploading any public artifact or deploying. The default is dry-run. Push builds remain disabled until `RFL_PAGES_ENABLED=true`. Push builds stay disabled until `RFL_PAGES_ENABLED=true`. A private preview artifact is accepted only for dry-run and can never be promoted.

The first real deployment must specify an explicit production artifact ID, normally supplied by the private workflow. There is no live receipt before the first deployment. On subsequent normal site pushes, the receiver uses `https://chipchirp.digital/rfl/deployment.json` to preserve the deployed game version. It revalidates the exact artifact and SHA against GitHub. There is no "latest build" selection.

Validate existing site pages, tools/submodules and CNAME in the first full dry run. Browser playtesting remains a separate release check. Before production, compare the private SHA to `/rfl/version.json` and `/rfl/deployment.json`. Browser JS is downloadable even when minified; the private development repository is what remains private.

## Retention and rollback

Browser artifacts expire after 90 days or a shorter configured repository limit. Renew by building a reviewed production release before expiry. Private runtime data lives in a durable private Release attachment; generated bytes never enter Git history. Expired/deleted artifacts fail site rebuilds closed while the existing live site remains intact. Do not remove RFL from the assembled site on a fetch error.

Rollback: manually supply an older unexpired production artifact ID, dry-run first, then `dry_run=false`. The current SHA is recorded in the published receipt. A successful private handoff is only a dispatch acknowledgement; verify the public deployment run separately. To disable the migration, unset `RFL_PAGES_ENABLED` and restore the original Pages branch/root source; this restores the original website without the artifact-only `/rfl/` path.

Local validation: receiver unit tests and both workflows' actionlint checks pass. No workflow was dispatched, Pages settings changed, release created, or merge performed during preparation.
